items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: I've heard her name crop up several times.

ctx.x: All right, well, Les Wilcox was an epileptic, but very few knew. And he always complained about a toothache, and he would drink gin to ease it. And hold gin in his mouth all night when he wasn't playing the horn. And he wrote music, like, individual parts. He didn't write scores. And he always would ask me to go home with him while they would write, keep him company, you know. And I would go with him, and tell him the truth on myself. We were smoking grass, then.

And he would write so he was exhausted and so I would go home and go to bed. Now, Kolax, who's true name was William Littles, they were supposed to come out here, under a banner of Ruth Ellington. But she decided not to make the trip. So Kolax and the band has already rehearsed and everything, and they had the uniforms and everything and at the last minute, she pulls out.
